$comment: Target branch-protection state for every public repository on this account.
ONE RULESET PER BRANCH, named protected-<branch>. A ruleset applies one set
of rules to every ref it covers, so main and dev cannot require different
checks inside a single one — and they routinely need to, because a CI
trigger often lists one branch and not the other.
NO BYPASS ACTOR. The rules apply to the owner exactly as they apply to a
contributor. That is only workable because required_approving_review_count
is 0: with a single collaborator GitHub forbids approving your own pull
request, so any non-zero count makes the rule unsatisfiable and forces a
bypass on every merge. The guarantee that nobody merges in your place is
not the review count — it is that nobody else has write access.
`checks` is a TARGET, not a promise. A required status check is matched by
context name; require one that never reports on that branch and every pull
request to it becomes permanently unmergeable, with 'Expected — Waiting for
status to be reported' and no error anywhere. apply-rulesets.sh therefore
only requires a context it has evidence for:
tier 1  a pull request targeting that branch has reported it
tier 2  a branch's `verified` field records a human reading the workflow
trigger and confirming it covers THAT branch, with the date
Anything with neither is withheld and printed. Re-run after a CI change.

GitKeeper.note: dev is excluded on purpose: it has diverged from main by 8 commits each way and carries only duplicated 'remove docs/' commits plus wiki pages that now live in the GitHub wiki. Protecting an abandoned branch documents it as live. Decide whether to delete it or reset it onto main.

dev.verified: 2026-09-09 — ci.yml: pull_request has no branches filter

Spifuth.note: The profile README repository. No workflow, so no check to require — the branch rules still block deletion, force-push and direct pushes.

AutoVault.note: tests.yml produces 12 contexts; only the aggregate 'CI Summary' is required. release.yml is deliberately absent — it triggers on v* tags only, so requiring it would block every pull request forever.

SockMap.note: The publish and release jobs live in the same workflow but carry an `if:` that skips them on a pull request, and a skipped check counts as passing — they are still not required, because a required context should not depend on a conditional staying conditional. The emoji are part of the context names: rename one and the requirement silently stops matching.

City-Compare.note: `release` reste hors des checks requis : il ne tourne jamais sur une pull request. `example-report` y est revenu le 2026-09-09 après City-Compare#4 : il appelle Nominatim et Open-Meteo, mais une panne de l'un ou l'autre sort désormais en EX_TEMPFAIL (75) et l'étape CI la traite comme un saut avec une annotation. Il ne peut donc plus échouer sur la disponibilité d'un tiers — seulement sur une vraie régression, ce qui est exactement ce qu'un check requis doit faire. Avant ce correctif il était retiré, et il avait raison de l'être.
